 JUDGMENT The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries suffered by him in a road accident dated 06.04.2023.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 06.04.2023 at about 10.30 to 10.35am when the petitioner was proceeding in a Honda Activa bearing No.KA-05-LE-8908 as a pillion rider and his friend Abhi J.C was riding the motorcycle on JP Nagar 1 st phase, Ayodhyarama Road, EG Circle towards Jayanagar very slowly, cautiously and observing all the traffic rules and regulations, a Car bearing No.KA-41-B-8523 came with high speed driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering human life, came from opposite direction and dashed against his motorcycle.
As a result, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, wherein admitted as an inpatient, underwent surgery, treated for 1 week and discharged with advice.

So far he has spent Rs.25,000/- towards conveyance,
food and nourishment charges.
Prior to the date of accident, he was hale and healthy and a student.
Due to accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled person.
The Jayanagara Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.No.110/2023 punishable u/Sec.279, 337 of IPC against the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-B-8523.
The 1 st respondent being the insurer and the 2 nd respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence this petition.
3. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent No.1 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.2 did not appear hence placed exparte.

4. Objection of the Respondent No.1.

sentences.text: It has denied all the averments of the petition.
It has denied the issuance of policy in favour of the 2nd respondent in respect of the Car bearing No.KA-41-B-8523.
The said offending Car did not have valid RC, Permit, Fitness Certificate at the time of accident.
There is one day delay in filing the FIR.
Further denied that the petitioner is a student.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 06.04.2023 at 10.30 to 10.35pm, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-B- 8523 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What order or Award?
6.
The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.11.
He has also got examined Dr.Vivekananda as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.12 to 14.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
8.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-B-8523, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments in his chief examination affidavit and produced 9 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.9.
During his cross-examination nothing worthwhile is elicited.
10. The accident occurred on 06.04.2023 at about 10.30 to 10.35am and the FIR at Ex.P.1 was registered on the next day i.e., on 07.04.2023 at 9.00pm on the complaint of the petitioner.
The spot Mahazar at Ex.P.2 was conducted on 08.04.2023 from 10.00am to 04.00pm.

The Sketch at Ex.P.3 Ravindra.R vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130785854/
3 shows the spot of the accident.

sentences.text: The IMV report at Ex.P.4 shows there was no fresh damages to the petitioner's vehicle bearing No.KA-05-EL-8908 and the offending vehicle Car bearing No.KA-41-B-8523 suffered damages to its right side body damaged near front fender.
Ex.P.5 is the notice sent to the RC owner of the offending vehicle with the details of the accident and also reply to the notice.
The Wound Certificate at Ex.P.6 shows that the petitioner has suffered injuries in RTA on 06.04.2023 at about 12.30pm and sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.7 is the police intimation and the police have filed the charge sheet after investigation at Ex.P.9 against the driver of the offending Car.
The Respondent No.1 has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have a valid DL and also the Car did not posses valid RC, FC and Permit.
But in order to prove the same they have neither produced any documents nor examined any witness.

Therefore, on the basis of the evidence of PW.1 and the documents before the court Exs.P.1 to P.9, the Tribunal holds that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle Car bearing No.KA-41-B-8523.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.6.

It shows that he suffered Swelling,
tenderness, crepitus, bony deformity of right mid thigh which are grievous in nature.
In support of his contention, he has examined the Doctor as PW.2 and got marked 3 documents i.e., case sheet, recent X-ray and OPD file as per Exs.P.12 to 14.
The doctor has given the details of the surgery in his chief examination that the petitioner was operated with CRIF with intramedulary interlocking nail for R femur shaft.
During the cross examination of the PW.2, he has stated that he is one of the Doctors who treated the petitioner.
The fracture is united and the accident took place one and half years ago.
The petitioner can do his job without any difficulties.
The petitioner is a BPL Card holder, they do not charge any money for removal of implants.

PW.2 has further stated that the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing his daily activities and has assessed the permanent disability of 35% for lower limb and to the whole body disability at 17%.

Disability:
12. On perusal of the evidence of PW.2 it is clear that the petitioner had suffered grievous injuries.

Due to the injuries, the petitioner is facing difficulty in walking for long distance and squatting,
walking on slope, climbing steps, sitting cross legged and sitting on knee and has pain in right leg.
However, the petitioner is young and he has to suffer the disability throughout his life.
Therefore, on the basis of the evidence of Pw.2, this tribunal deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 15%.
Age of the Petitioner 13.
The Petitioner, in order to prove his age, has produced notarized copy of Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.10.
As per the said document, his date of birth is 15.07.2005.
The accident occurred on 06.04.2023.
As such, as on the date of accident the age of the Petitioner is considered as 17 years 8 Ravindra.

4 months 22 days.
 Quantum of Income and quantum of compensation 14.
The Petitioner, as on the date of accident, admittedly was a minor.
Therefore, he was not earning anything.

As per the decision of Hon'ble supreme court reported in ILR 2014 Kar 4891 rendered in Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance having regard to relevant factors,
precedents and approach of various Hon'ble High Courts with regard to the compensation of the child victims, held that appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc., should be Rs.1,00,000/- disability up to 10%, if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to whole body 3 lakhs: up to 60% 4 lakhs: up to 90% 5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be 6 lakhs.

sentences.text:
Therefore,
the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- under the head of pain and suffering already undergone including loss of comforts amenities on account of disability.

15. The Petitioner was inpatient from 16.04.2023 to 12.04.2023, diagnosed and treated to the post traumatic closed right femur shaft fracture with no neurovascular deficits with a procedure of CRIF with IMIL NAILING FOR RIGHT FEMUR and discharged with follow up treatment.
This must have caused loss of some income and discomforts to the parents of the Petitioner during that period.
Therefore, his parents are entitled for a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the heads of loss of income and discomforts to the parents.
During the treatment the guardian of the petitioner must have spent considerable amount towards his conveyance and nourishment etc.,
Therefore, Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
The PW.1 stated that he has spent Rs.25,000/- towards medical expenses.
In this regard the Petitioner has produced 5 medical bills as per Ex.P.11 for a sum of Rs.9,685/-.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondents.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.9,685/- under the heads of medical expenses.
PW.2 has stated that, the petitioner is in need of treatment for removal of implants and the approximate cost of the treatment is around Rs.40,000/- to Rs.50,000/-.
In this regard the PW.2 or the petitioner have not produced any estimation bill.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the Future Medical Expenses at Rs.20,000/-

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-

 undergone and to be suffered in  future including loss of comforts  amenities on account of  disability.

5. Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/-

If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.3,90,000/- and the same is awarded to the petitioner under different heads.

16. LIABILITY:
As discussed above the Respondents have failed to prove their defence about the accident.
Therefore, the Respondents Nos.1 & 2 being the insurer and the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs. 3,90,000/- alongwith interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,90,000/-. (Rupees Three Lakhs Ninety Thousand only) along with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount by the respondent.
The Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
